concept.name: ETL vs. ELT Data Pipelines

relationships.description: Connects ETL vs ELT Pipelines to data warehousing lakehouse in the broader engineering catalog.

concept.tagline: Deciding whether to transform data in-flight before storage (ETL) or land raw payloads first and transform in-place inside cloud warehouses (ELT).
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of ETL vs. ELT—from why cloud storage/compute separation flipped the default to how Medallion lakehouses combine pre-load PII redaction with in-place SQL transforms.

spark.summary: ETL transforms raw data on dedicated compute servers before loading it into a target warehouse, whereas ELT loads raw data directly into scalable cloud storage and transforms it in-place using warehouse SQL/compute.
spark.keyTakeaway: Modern cloud data platforms favor ELT for schema agility and raw-history replayability, reserving pre-load ETL for strict PII redaction, high-frequency stream aggregation, and regulatory compliance.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Every analytical pipeline performs three verbs: **Extract** bytes from operational sources (Postgres, Kafka, SaaS APIs), **Transform** them (deduplicate, cast types, mask PII, join dimensions), and **Load** them into an analytical store.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts ETL (Transform In-Flight) vs. ELT (Land Raw, Transform In-Place) (OLTP / Kafka -> Spark / Beam -> Cloud Warehouse -> Silver / Gold BI); Hybrid CDC Pre-Filter + Iceberg Bronze/Silver/Gold (Postgres WAL + Debezium -> Iceberg Bronze (Raw) -> dbt Silver (Clean) -> dbt Gold (Marts)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Beyond classic ETL and SQL-driven ELT, cloud vendors now offer **Zero-ETL** (managed CDC replication directly from Aurora/DynamoDB into Redshift/BigQuery) and **Medallion Hybrid** architectures. High-scale data platforms blend both patterns: a lightweight CDC/ETL proxy strips or tokenizes PII in flight and lands immutable Parquet into **Iceberg Bronze**, while **dbt**.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore how CDC pipelines, Medallion lakehouses, and open table formats implement reliable ETL and ELT in production.

learningJourney.title: What is ETL vs. ELT
learningJourney.explanation:
Every analytical pipeline performs three verbs: **Extract** bytes from operational sources (Postgres, Kafka, SaaS APIs), **Transform** them (deduplicate, cast types, mask PII, join dimensions), and **Load** them into an analytical store. The sole architectural distinction between **ETL** and **ELT** is **where and when Transform runs**.

In **ETL** (Extract → Transform → Load), transformation happens *in flight* on a dedicated external cluster (Spark, Flink, Informatica, AWS Glue) before the target database sees a row. In **ELT** (Extract → Load → Transform), raw JSON/Parquet is loaded *immediately* into a cloud warehouse or lakehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Iceberg), and transformations execute *in place* via distributed SQL or DataFrame engines (dbt, Spark SQL).

sectionDiagram.title: ETL (Transform In-Flight) vs. ELT (Land Raw, Transform In-Place)
sectionDiagram.summary: ETL cleans data before persistence to protect the target store; ELT persists immutable raw history first so SQL transforms can be replayed anytime.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how ETL vs. ELT works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Cloud Economics Flipped ETL to ELT
learningJourney.explanation: Traditional ETL protected expensive, compute-constrained on-premise appliances (Oracle, Teradata) by cleaning and aggregating data before ingestion—but any change in business logic meant re-running upstream pipelines from source systems. Modern cloud warehouses separate cheap object storage (~$20–$23/TB/month) from elastic compute, making ELT (Airbyte/Debezium + dbt) the default: land raw payloads in minutes and iterate on SQL models without touching upstream APIs.

ideas.title: Raw-History Replayability
ideas.description: ELT preserves immutable staging tables (`bronze` layer). If a SQL join has a timezone bug, engineers fix the dbt model and re-materialize `silver`/`gold` tables without re-extracting from OLTP databases.

ideas.title: Compliance & Volume Boundaries
ideas.description: Pure ELT fails when GDPR/HIPAA forbids raw SSNs or PANs from touching the lakehouse, or when 500k+ events/sec of noisy IoT telemetry must be downsampled before warehouse ingestion.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Why Cloud Economics Flipped ETL to ELT under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where to Use ELT, Pre-Load ETL, or Hybrid Medallion
learningJourney.explanation: Choosing between ETL and ELT depends on schema volatility, data volume, and regulatory boundaries rather than dogma.

benefits: Landing data into Snowflake, BigQuery, or Iceberg when analytical metrics evolve weekly and data scientists need raw event payloads.
costs: Duplicates data across Bronze/Silver/Gold layers; unoptimized `dbt run` full refreshes burn warehouse credits.

benefits: Drops noisy IoT readings (cutting ingestion bills by 80%) and tokenizes HIPAA/PCI-DSS PII before disk persistence.
costs: Schema changes or attribution backfills require modifying external Spark/Beam code and re-extracting upstream.

comparison.choice: Avoid Pure ELT: Legacy OLTP Targets
benefits: Offloads heavy `MERGE` and `JOIN` compute to an external Spark/Glue cluster.
costs: Running massive ELT `MERGE` queries inside a constrained OLTP appliance starves live transactional queries.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Incremental ELT Merges & Pre-Load PII Redaction
learningJourney.explanation: Production pipelines prevent runaway warehouse bills and late-data skew by using **rolling lookback windows** keyed on `_loaded_at` in incremental `dbt` models, paired with explicit column allowlists or deterministic HMAC tokenization in pre-load ETL.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Traditional ETL vs. Modern ELT vs. Zero-ETL
learningJourney.explanation: Beyond classic ETL and SQL-driven ELT, cloud vendors now offer **Zero-ETL** (managed CDC replication directly from Aurora/DynamoDB into Redshift/BigQuery) and **Medallion Hybrid** architectures.

benefits: Minutes to land raw data; version-controlled SQL transforms with `not_null` and `unique` tests.
costs: Without catalog governance and resource monitors, raw schemas become an undocumented data swamp.

benefits: Enforces strict PII tokenization and high-throughput stream filtering before analytical storage.
costs: Slower schema evolution; requires maintaining external JVM/Python cluster autoscaling.

benefits: Eliminates custom ingestion connectors for single-cloud OLTP-to-warehouse sync.
costs: Tightly couples to one cloud vendor and offers limited pre-load PII filtering.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Hybrid Medallion: Debezium + Iceberg Bronze + dbt
learningJourney.explanation: High-scale data platforms blend both patterns: a lightweight CDC/ETL proxy strips or tokenizes PII in flight and lands immutable Parquet into **Iceberg Bronze**, while **dbt** runs incremental SQL transformations to materialize **Silver** and **Gold** tables.

sectionDiagram.title: Hybrid CDC Pre-Filter + Iceberg Bronze/Silver/Gold

cards.label: Pre-Load Guard
cards.detail: Debezium/Beam drops password_hash and HMAC-tokenizes SSNs before S3 persistence.

cards.label: Bronze Replay
cards.detail: Raw events stay immutable in Iceberg so buggy Silver/Gold SQL can be backfilled anytime.

cards.label: Cost Control
cards.detail: Partitioned incremental MERGEs with 3-day lookback avoid 10 TB full-table scans.

sectionDiagram.summary: Use lightweight ETL at the ingestion boundary for PII and noise reduction, and ELT inside the lakehouse for agile business modeling.

knowledgeCheck.question: A health-tech team ingests HL7/FHIR claims into BigQuery for analytics, but HIPAA forbids storing unencrypted SSNs in the analytical warehouse. Which architecture satisfies both compliance and agile SQL modeling?

options.text: Pure ELT: land raw payloads in BigQuery Bronze and mask SSNs later in dbt Silver
options.feedback: Pure ELT stores raw unencrypted SSNs in the Bronze table, violating HIPAA at rest.

options.text: Hybrid ETL+ELT: hash/tokenize SSNs in a stateless Beam/Dataflow pre-load stage, then run dbt ELT in BigQuery
options.feedback: Correct: pre-load ETL enforces PII tokenization before persistence while keeping downstream SQL modeling agile.

options.text: Run nightly full-table refreshes in BigQuery without partitioning
options.feedback: Full-table refreshes do not solve PII storage compliance and cause runaway warehouse compute costs.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
